Nowadays in my country, direct-from-china furnitures are way cheaper than Ikea’s for the scale and size they are selling. It’s also flat-packed, and sent using ocean freight, but it’s way cheaper than equivalent Ikea’s. I used some of them for furniture that I just need something usable or temporary….

But if I want quality for cheap, Ikea is still the way to go. The QA is just great. All the chinese furnitures comes in very thin cardboard, and more often than not come with broken pieces or bent metal. It’s fine if I just want something cheap that can hold things, but if I need something trusted, I trust Ikea.

comments.text:
Outside of Tokyo, so many people drive, so the idea of the big-box store or mall is so common here now. IKEA had a sign in 2011 in the dirt lot next to the Costco in Gunma, and they finally opened it in 2025, along with a giant Uniqlo sharing the pad. 

It may have cramped parking lots, but the large strip malls with a department store and Supermarket, across the street from a Costco and an IKEA surrounded by chain shops with a Starbucks & McDonalds next to a tollway exit - with no train access - is reality in Maebashi today. I think Japanese culture changed a lot from the 60s to be more in line with western tastes IKEA could fill - shopping at Costco on Saturday and loading your giant haul of groceries into a huge minivan is now a common thing for many people here.
